reader.decision: Approve the 600-second TTL in reorder.py and the us-east switch to lock_backend: redis, conditional on confirming that Redis host redis-locks is reachable from us-east. Treat the idempotent purchase order key as a follow-up hardening item.
reader.decision_reason: The message shows that both regions fail to prevent overlap: eu-west's 60s TTL is shorter than the 4-minute job, and us-east has no lock at all. Since nobody knows which region ran the duplicate, the fix has to cover both. The proposed change is small and stays inside the repository. The only open risk is Redis reachability from us-east, which I can check before merging.

reconstruction.problem: restock-planner's reorder job sent Halvorsen Tools two purchase orders for SKU HT-4410. The reorder lock does not cover the roughly 4-minute job. In eu-west the Redis lock has a 60s TTL, so it expires mid-run. In us-east lock_backend is none, so acquire always returns True. A second pod (B) started at 01:02 after a node restart and ran alongside pod A.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Two pods run reorder at the same time and both create a purchase order for the same item, so the supplier gets duplicate orders. This assumes HT-4410 was still below its reorder point at 01:02. The message could not check that because purchasing is outside the repository.
reconstruction.fix: Change ttl_seconds from 60 to 600 in planner/reorder.py. Change config/us-east.yaml from lock_backend: none to redis. Leave eu-west.yaml unchanged. The alternative is an idempotent create_purchase_order keyed on SKU plus run date, which needs a change in purchasing.
reconstruction.cost: A pod that crashes mid-run blocks the next attempt for up to 10 minutes. us-east now depends on Redis being reachable, and the message cannot confirm that redis-locks serves both regions. A job longer than 10 minutes would still duplicate. The idempotent-key alternative needs a change in purchasing, which is not in this repository.

follow_up_questions: Is the redis-locks host reachable from us-east pods, and is it the intended lock store for that region?
Can anything confirm that HT-4410 was still below its reorder point at 01:02, for example purchasing logs or order timestamps?
reader.closing_answer: I approve the 600-second TTL and the us-east Redis lock, provided redis-locks is reachable from us-east. I will check that connectivity before merging. I will also track the idempotent purchase order key as a follow-up in purchasing, since it protects against any lock failure and covers jobs longer than 10 minutes.
